title: Policy election debug breadcrumbs
content:
Summary:

Quick personal scratchpad capturing the command trail, log snippets, and hypotheses from the regional failover that started 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC. Focus is on the policy-election path (how the routing layer chose fallback model/region), why the TTL-based re-election fired repeatedly, and why traffic transiently split across two regions despite expected single-winner elections.

What I saw (high level):
- Traffic from eu-west started shifting to us-east via fallback policy between 02:14–02:22 UTC.
- Routing logs show two concurrent election winners for ~20s for the same customer keyspace: leader=eu-west-1 and leader=us-east-1.
- Decisions appear driven by the election TTL expiring and a re-entrant election happening during partial cache eviction.

Timeline + commands (local terminal history + outputs)

2026-03-10 02:16:12 UTC — started watching the live election state (redis-backed election index):
$ redis-cli -h election-redis-01 GET election:customer:acme-42
"{"leader":"eu-west-1","seq":10233,"expires_at":1678432578}"

02:16:34 — on router-03 (eu-west) pulled current in-memory route table snapshot:
$ curl -sS http://localhost:9001/internal/route_table | jq '.policies["acme-42"]'
{
  "policy_id": "fallback-compact-v3",
  "strategy": "weighted-consistent-hash",
  "candidates": ["eu-west-1","us-east-1"],
  "weights": {"eu-west-1":0.9,"us-east-1":0.1},
  "election_ttl_s": 10
}

02:17:05 — observed rapid re-election events in routing log (snippet):
[2026-03-10T02:17:05.127Z] INFO election: started election for acme-42 (seq=10234)
[2026-03-10T02:17:05.129Z] INFO election: winner=us-east-1 (lease acquired)
[2026-03-10T02:17:05.145Z] INFO election: started election for acme-42 (seq=10235)
[2026-03-10T02:17:05.149Z] INFO election: winner=eu-west-1 (lease acquired)

02:17:06 — grabbed tcpdump around router handoffs to see in-flight requests hitting both regions: (trimmed)
$ sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/election.pcap port 443 and host acme-42-client
... multiple SYN/ACK flows to us-east and eu-west in same second ...

Immediate checks I ran
- Confirmed election-redis latency:
$ redis-cli -h election-redis-01 --latency
* (latency samples) 3/200/12/48 ms
(note: occasional 48ms spikes at 02:16:50)

- Checked router GC/log rotation around 02:16:
$ journalctl -u redwood-router -S "2026-03-10 02:15" -U "2026-03-10 02:20" | grep -i "election" | sed -n '1,120p'
(see snippet above)

- Looked for lock-contend or watch/unwatch jitter on election key (we use SETNX+PEXPIRE pattern)
$ redis-cli -h election-redis-01 GET election:lock:acme-42
(nil)

Observed error/odd snippets
- Occasionally see 'LeaseAlreadyHeld' followed by 'LeaseAcquired' without intervening release logs:
[2026-03-10T02:17:05.128Z] WARN election: LeaseAlreadyHeld by eu-west-1 for acme-42 (seq=10233)
[2026-03-10T02:17:05.129Z] INFO election: winner=us-east-1 (lease acquired)

- TTL math appears off by ~100ms in logs — expires_at sometimes a hair earlier than local clock leading to immediate re-elections. Example: expires_at=1678432578, local ts=1678432578.08 => race.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Clock skew between routers (eu-west vs us-east) leading to near-simultaneous elections. Even small skews (<200ms) cause both nodes to believe lease expired and try to acquire.
   - Evidence: expires_at vs local timestamp mismatch; rapid winner flips across regions.
   - Quick check: NTP drift table on router-03 shows 130ms jump around 02:16:50.

2) Redis SETNX+PEXPIRE sequence exposure: clients are doing SETNX then PEXPIRE not atomically — under high latency a second client may see key absent briefly and succeed concurrently.
   - Evidence: occasional 48ms redis latency spike; LeaseAlreadyHeld + LeaseAcquired pairing.
   - Mitigation note: prefer SET key PX NX pattern to set TTL atomically.

3) In-memory routing table update lag: the control loop that applies election result to the local route table may be out-of-order; a late writer patches the table and triggers a re-election cycle because cached candidate weights are stale.
   - Evidence: application logs show apply->ack delays about 80ms at same time window.

4) Heartbeat / health-check thrashing: an instance in eu-west reported soft-degraded (CPU burst) causing router weight to momentarily drop then recover, triggering election voter recalculation.
   - Evidence: node-level metrics showed CPU spike on infra-eu-west-02 at 02:16:42.

Quick repro attempts I tried
- Simulate small clock skew: on a test staging pair, used sudo date -s "+120ms" then triggered elections with a gold key. Observed both claim victory intermittently. Reconfirmed hypothesis (1).

- Replayed redis latency by tc qdisc netem to election-redis and saw transient dual-winner condition when redis latency > 40ms.

Notes on config/code to change (ideas):
- Switch to SET key value PX <ms> NX (atomic TTL) for lease acquisition instead of SETNX+PEXPIRE.
- Add a short randomized jitter (20–50ms) before re-trying an election when lease observed expired to reduce simultaneous tries (backoff window bounded by election_ttl).
- Increase election_ttl_s from 10 -> 30 for high-latency cross-region customers to avoid thrash; (but measure impact on failover speed).
- Add a small HLC-style hybrid logical timestamp inserted into the lease value so nodes can detect ‘recently expired but still valid’ windows.

Local TODO (next steps)
- [ ] Push a patch to routing-election library to use atomic SET PX NX + GET to confirm winner (PR started, WIP). Refer PR: https://github.com/redwood/realtime-routing/pull/312
- [ ] Instrument redis roundtrip histogram (client-side) to get percentiles during incidents (Rajiv to own)
- [ ] Run chaos test in staging that injects 50–100ms ntp skew and 40ms redis latency to validate mitigations
- [ ] Add a rule in incident runbook: if dual-winner > 10s, escalate to platform-engineering-sre and increase election_ttl for the flagged policy

Misc notes + artifacts captured:
- pcap saved: /tmp/election-2026-03-10.pcap (filtered for acme-42)
- route table snapshot saved: /var/tmp/route-snap-2026-03-10-eu-west.json
- redis dump partial: /tmp/election-dump-acme-42.txt

Thoughts for post-mortem framing:
- Root cause likely composite: small clock skew + non-atomic lease set + redis latency spike. Single root-cause call would be misleading; emphasize emergent property of components.
- Actionable immediate fix: atomic SET PX NX + 30ms jitter on retries. Medium term: HLC timestamps or leader-confirmation gossip protocol to avoid split winners.

If/when I get to it, I want to graph around the incident:
- election wins time series (region labels) at 50ms resolution
- redis latency heatmap across cluster nodes
- NTP offset timeseries for routers

---
End of scratchpad. Leaving raw outputs and traces in my home dir for reproducibility.

A.
